question.knowledge_point: Finding the Area Bounded by a Curve, the y-Axis, and Two Horizontal Lines
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013903/assets/b4408c4dc92d7145fef94603269f2cc54ceeb3bb38703401ff46004a2428dd3f.png)

Find the area bounded between the curve $x=-{y}^{5}+1,$ the $y$-axis, and the lines $y=0$ and $y=1,$ as shown above.
question.worked_solution:
To find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(-{y}^{5}+1)\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{5}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & =-{\frac{{y}^{6}}{6}|}_{0}^{1}+y{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =-(\frac{1}{6}-0)+(1-0) \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}+1 \\  & =\frac{5}{6}\end{aligned}
$$
